jonah.3.p1.b1.text: Then the word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:

jonah.3.p1.b2.text: “Get up! Go to the great city of Nineveh and proclaim to it the message that I give you.”

jonah.3.p1.b3.text: This time Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, in accordance with the word of the LORD.

jonah.3.p2.b1.text: Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, requiring a three-day journey.

jonah.3.p2.b2.text: On the first day of his journey, Jonah set out into the city

jonah.3.p3.b1.text: “Forty more days and Nineveh will be overturned!”

jonah.3.p3.b2.text: And the Ninevites believed God. They proclaimed a fast and dressed in sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least.

jonah.3.p4.b1.text: When word reached the king of Nineveh

jonah.3.p4.b2.text: he got up from his throne, took off his royal robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

jonah.3.p4.b3.text: Then he issued a proclamation in Nineveh:

jonah.3.p4.b4.text: “By the decree of the king and his nobles: Let no man or beast, herd or flock, taste anything at all. …

jonah.3.p5.b1.text: … They must not eat or drink. … Furthermore, let both man and beast be covered with sackcloth

jonah.3.p5.b2.text: Let each one turn from his evil ways and from the violence in his hands.

jonah.3.p5.b3.text: Who knows? God may turn and relent; He may turn from His fierce anger, so that we will not perish.”

jonah.3.p5.b4.text: When God saw their actions—that they had turned from their evil ways—He relented from the disaster He had threatened to bring upon them.
